comments.author: Narcotics
comments.body_html: Would it be possible to add a “Disable” option to flashlights/lasers that would cause them to not turn on when the keybind is pressed? Would come in handy if you’re running a white light during a night raid and only want to use IR, while still having the capability of white light when needed.

comments.author: IcyClawz
comments.body_html:
You’re commenting on a library that doesn’t add anything on its own…

Also, adding keybinds is not the purpose of this library.

comments.author: Narcotics
comments.body_html:
I meant to comment on your other mod, “Item Context Menu Extended” - didn’t realize till just now, my apologies!

I do not mean to add a keybind, I mean to add a context menu option that basically disables that flashlight/laser until it is enabled again via the context menu. Would be useful when running a light/laser combo and you want to switch between having white light capability or just using the IR from the laser.

comments.author: IcyClawz
comments.body_html: I have no idea what you mean, or what prevents you from already being able to do that using “Item Context Menu Extended”.

comments.author: Narcotics
comments.body_html:
Item Context Menu Extended allows you to turn on or turn off the light/laser, I am requesting an option to disable the attachment entirely essentially until it gets re-enabled again via the context menu. This is just a QoL instead of the alternative of always having the IR on/flashlight off or vice versa.

For example, say you have an IR laser with a white light combo during a night raid - you are running a pair of nods, so you do not need the white light majority of the time. You could disable the flashlight in the beginning of the raid, so now every time you press your tactical keybind - only the IR laser turns on (because the flashlight has been disabled). During that raid, you get into situations where your nods are not ideal and you would like to use white light - you could then re-enable the flashlight via the context menu and it would continue to function as normal (the light turns on when the tactical keybind is pressed).

Totally understand if this is too big of an ask or outside of the scope of what you would like to achieve with your mod though, sorry for all of the confusion!

comments.author: IcyClawz
comments.body_html:
I just don’t understand the use case.

What’s the difference between “turn on or turn off the light/laser” and “disable the attachment entirely”? You can already turn on/off and switch between the mods per attachment…

comments.author: Narcotics
comments.body_html:
I’ll try to provide a scenario to see if it helps understand.

So we start our night raid with a nice little kitted out M4 with a PEQ -15 on its IR laser setting and an Ultrafire flashlight (which only has white light) - both of them are turned off. We are running nods as well.

Any time I want to use my laser, I also must use my flashlight (because pressing the keybind will turn both of them on). I would like to only use my laser though. The only option you have in raid is to either run a laser on constantly with the flashlight turned off, so every time you turn the laser off, the flashlight turns on (running a beam or light constantly essentially).

So if I have both attachments turned off, they both must turn on to use them. Being able to disable them via the context menu allows you the option of running one or the other dynamically in raid.

So we start our raid with same stuff, same settings (IR laser setting/white light flashlight setting) , both turned off. You would then be able to disable the flashlight attachment and only use the IR laser for when nod conditions are ideal and the white light isn’t really needed. But say we approach a well-lit street, building, area, etc and we want to switch to having white light capability? We could go into the context menu and re-enable the flashlight. So now when we press our keybind, we get the white light. If we slip back into the darkness and no longer need the white light? We could disable it again, so now when we press the keybind we are only using our IR laser once more.

The only alternative currently is either running one on and one off constantly - or going into the context menu and manually turning it off after every time you press the keybind, which is obviously not ideal in combat situations.

I hope this helps clarfiy, I’m so bad at explaining shit

comments.author: IcyClawz
comments.body_html: Disabling attachments as if they don’t really exist on the weapon is not a thing.
